findings.title: What-if rate limiter is skipped on every failing return of async_simulate
findings.claim: A what-if whose shadow solve raises returns without setting _last_simulation, so the rate limiter never engages and each further simulate_plan call launches another full solve: 5 calls start 5 solves where the success path starts 1.
findings.mechanism: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_simulate (coordinator.py:10537) sets self._last_simulation = now only on the success return (coordinator.py:10751). The three other returns - {"error": str(err)} at coordinator.py:10700 after the shadow solve raises, invalid_windows, and wood_err - leave the slot empty. #783's WORKER_FALLBACK_CAP makes _await_optimize raise UpdateFailed on every solve once the process worker has failed four times running, so an install whose child interpreter cannot start re-solves on every dashboard slider drag, in the very process whose worker is already unusable.

evidence.contention_note: Shared fan-out box, load1 6.46; the metric is a call count, not a timing, so contention does not move it.

perturbation.change: One-line production edit: insert `self._last_simulation = now` immediately before `return {"error": str(err), "rate_limited": False}` at coordinator.py:10700.

findings.metric_definition: Shadow-solve submissions, counted at the production _await_process seam, across 5 consecutive async_simulate calls with the clock frozen and the rate-limit slot left untouched.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every return path of a rate-limited entry point must consume the rate-limit slot, not only its success path.
findings.seam_rule: Enumerate the returns of coordinator.py:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_simulate; every one that can follow a scheduled solve must set _last_simulation.

null_control.note: The same five calls with the shadow solve succeeding (RESULT simulate_solves_after_5_successful_calls=1): the effect vanishes exactly where the solve succeeds, so the count is a property of the failing return path and not of the call loop.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py async_simulate: set self._last_simulation = now on every return that follows a scheduled solve (the error return at :10700 at minimum). Roughly one line plus its comment.

findings.title: Stale-plan actuation gate covers the switch path but not the circulation-pump path
findings.claim: _plan_is_stale is consulted by _apply_action only; a stale plan still drives _async_drive_pumps, so 1 of the 2 actuating write paths in the same tick writes to the plant from a horizon the plan has been declared unfit to actuate.
findings.mechanism: _apply_action (coordinator.py:6560) returns early when _mode is AUTO/ECONOMY and _plan_is_stale(), and its docstring states the rule: the pump's own weather-compensated curve holds comfort instead. _async_drive_pumps (coordinator.py:2590) is called one statement later in _async_update_data with no staleness test; it derives idx from now - result.timestamps[0] and lets pump_schedule.plan_commands_heat clamp it to n-1, so an expired plan is read at its last step and the pumps keep being commanded from it. The direction is the safe one (curve_driven from the same stale _current_action forces the space pump ON), which is why this is low rather than high.

evidence.unit: actuating write paths still writing when the plan is stale
evidence.contention_note: Shared fan-out box, load1 6.46; a call count under the frozen clock, immune to contention.

perturbation.change: One-line production edit: insert `if self._mode in (MODE_AUTO, MODE_ECONOMY) and self._plan_is_stale(): return` at the top of _async_drive_pumps (coordinator.py:2590).

findings.metric_definition: Of the actuating write paths driven with _plan_is_stale() true, how many still reach a hass.services.async_call or _async_set_pump.
findings.phenomenon_property: A guard that withdraws actuation authority from an expired plan must cover every write path in the same tick, not one of them.
findings.seam_rule: Enumerate the write paths _async_update_data drives after the solve (the statement list following `boost.apply(self)`, coordinator.py:4479); each must consult _plan_is_stale before it commands the plant.

null_control.note: The same paths with a fresh plan: fresh_paths_detail={'heat_pump_switch': 1, 'space_pump': 2}, i.e. every path writes when the plan is current -- so the count is a property of the stale gate, not of the drive loop.

reproduction_steps: read RESULT actuating_paths_stale_gated=1, actuating_paths_still_writing_when_stale=1 and RESULT stale_paths_detail={'space_pump': 2}
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py _async_drive_pumps: consult _plan_is_stale (or have _async_update_data skip the pump drive on the same early-return branch _apply_action uses). One guard line.
